newsitem.title: CANADA: INSTANT VIEW - Canada CPI rises 2.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Canada CPI rises 2.0 pct.

text.p: Following are reactions to a rise of 2.0 percent in Canada's consumer price index for the month of November, released by Statistics Canada on Wednesday.
Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast a 1.7 percent rise, on average.

MICHAEL GREGORY, SENIOR ECONOMIST AT LEHMAN BROTHERS IN TORONTO: "It was a little bit higher than expected. But a lot of that is oil and the all items, but the core is still 1.4 percent, which is perfectly fine. I think we're seeing the impact of higher energy prices starting to feed through.
SAL GUATIERI, SENIOR ECONOMIST, BANK OF MONTREAL

"The measure was boosted a bit by higher gasoline prices, however it looks like it's also been boosted by higher auto insurance premiums and as well the core measure of inflation moved up unexpectedly to 1.4 percent. It's looking like it reflects higher university tuition fees and higher rental costs as well. There is some price pressure in certain areas of the economy, especially regulated prices such as university tuition. Is this the beginning of a reversal from a downward (inflation) trend? We don't think so. We think there is sufficient slack and unused capacity in the economy to keep inflation if not on a downward course at least stabilised."
